column3: “For righteousness … for justice” is rendered with adverbs, “righteously … justly.”
“Will not gaze” is rendered “will not be blinded,” following a different vowel reading.
“His heart does wickedness” is rendered “his heart inclines toward wickedness.”
“Words of falsehood” is rendered “slander,” and “when the needy speaks justice” as “Even though the needy one speaks what is right.”
“Days with a year” is rendered “Within a year and a few days,” and “will fail” as “is ended.”
“Mourning on breasts” is rendered “Beat your breasts.”
“Will be forsaken” is rendered in the past, “has been abandoned”; “the tumult of the city” as “the populated city.”
“How blessed you are” is rendered “will you be,” and “let loose the foot” as “let out freely.”
